_comment: The historical clock. Each event fires once, when its day arrives, and sets the flags listed. Text is the news as it reaches the Cadurci hills. Day 1 is the Cenabum massacre, about 9 January 52 BC; day numbers follow docs/research/chronology-52bc.md.

events.title: News from the Arverni
events.text: A potter coming down from the north says Vercingetorix, the young Arvernian noble whose own uncle threw him out of Gergovia, came back with an army of the poor and the desperate and drove out every elder who told him to wait. They call him king now. The potter says he's handsome. The potter is not a reliable witness.

events.title: A rider in the hills
events.text: Lucterius of the Cadurci is riding from hall to hall, calling men to the revolt in Vercingetorix's name. Every hearth in the hills is arguing about it. Every hearth in Brigodunon is thinking about three hostages.

events.title: The king marches
events.text: Vercingetorix has marched north into the country of the Bituriges with most of his army, to bring them into the war whether they like it or not. Behind him in Gergovia he left a garrison, his hostages, and a row of black stakes on the plateau where the men who said wait were burned.

events.title: Caesar in the snow
events.text: Caesar has crossed the Cevennes through snow six feet deep, where everyone agreed no army could go, and his horsemen are burning Arvernian farms. In his own account he will call this a demonstration of Roman diligence. The farmers have another word for it.

events.title: Caesar on the Liger
events.text: Caesar has come north with his legions faster than anyone thought an army could move in winter. He took Vellaunodunum of the Senones in three days and is marching on Cenabum, to punish the Carnutes for the massacre. Everyone between here and the Liger is packing.

events.title: Cenabum empties
events.text: Word from the Liger: when the news of Vellaunodunum reached Cenabum, Senuacos didn't wait for dark. He stood in the market at noon with his staff and sent the town out by daylight, family by family, upstream and down and over the old ways, and by nightfall Cenabum was empty but for the dogs.

events.title: Cenabum
events.text: Caesar reached Cenabum at nightfall and found the gates open and nobody to shut them. He burned it anyway, and gave what was left to his soldiers, and crossed the Liger into the country of the Bituriges.

events.title: Cenabum
events.text: Caesar reached Cenabum at nightfall. The townsmen tried to slip out over the bridge in the dark, all of them at once, and the bridge was narrow. The legions were waiting at the gate. Cenabum is burned, and the people who were in it are sold or dead.

events.title: Smoke in the north
events.text: The Bituriges have burned more than twenty of their own towns in a single day, so Caesar's army would find nothing to eat. They begged to spare Avaricum, the most beautiful city in Gaul, and the council let them.

events.title: Avaricum
events.text: Caesar has come up against Avaricum and dug in on the south side, the one side the river and the marsh leave open. Vercingetorix is camped sixteen miles off in the marshes, and he has sent ten thousand picked men into the city. The roads into Avaricum are watched now, by one side or the other, and it has started to rain.

events.title: The assembly
events.text: The roads have dried, and the Cadurci of Brigodunon have met in assembly without you. Lucterius's man spoke, and nobody who had been to Noviodunum was there to answer him. Vellaunos will tell you how it went.

events.title: Avaricum
events.text: Avaricum has fallen. Those who got out say the Romans spared no one: not the old, not the women, not the children. Of about forty thousand people, some eight hundred reached Vercingetorix's camp.

events.title: Talk among the Aedui
events.text: A trader up from the Liger says the Aedui are quarrelling. Two men claimed the chief magistracy and Caesar had to come to Decetia to settle it, and the young men of the losing side talk about the Arverni a great deal more than they used to.

events.title: Caesar at Gergovia
events.text: Caesar has crossed the Elaver by a trick, rebuilding one of the broken bridges on its old piles while the men watching the river followed the rest of his army downstream, and come up to Gergovia in five marches. He has camped under the mountain. Vercingetorix holds the slopes behind a wall of stone six feet high, and the camps of every people in the revolt are spread along the heights like washing.

events.title: The Aeduan column
events.text: Ten thousand Aeduan foot are on the road to join Caesar under a young noble named Litaviccus. Thirty miles from Gergovia he stopped them and wept, and told them Caesar had murdered their nobles. He had witnesses. The witnesses had been paid. The Roman citizens marching under the column's protection were taken out and tortured to death, and the grain went with them.

events.title: Riot at Cabillonum
events.text: The rumor from the column reached the Aeduan towns before the truth did. At Cabillonum on the Arar they plundered the Roman traders, then promised the tribune Aristius and the merchants safe conduct out of town and fell on them on the road. The Romans held out for a day and a night. Then the truth arrived, and the same men who had done it went to Caesar to say how sorry they were.

events.title: Caesar beaten
events.text: Caesar has been beaten under the walls of Gergovia. For the first time in six years, the legions are the ones retreating.

events.title: The Aedui turn
events.text: The Aedui, Rome's oldest friends in Gaul, have thrown over Caesar. They seized his depot at Noviodunum, killed the garrison, and took the hostages, the grain and the pay chest to Bibracte. Somewhere in that baggage are the children of half the peoples of Gaul.

events.title: Horsemen from over the Rhine
events.text: Caesar has sent across the Rhine for German horsemen and light foot, and finding their ponies poor, mounted them on the horses of his own officers. Vercingetorix answers by sending the Cadurci and the Ruteni south to raid the Volcae Arecomici in the Province. Lucterius's riders are in the hills again, counting young men.

events.title: The council of all Gaul
events.text: Every people in the revolt has sent its men to Bibracte, and the Aedui, who called the council because they wanted the command, have watched the whole of Gaul vote it to Vercingetorix instead. They submitted. Nobody who was there thinks they liked it.

events.title: Alesia
events.text: Vercingetorix threw his horse at Caesar's column on the march and swore his riders not to come home unless they had ridden through it twice. The Germans took the ridge, and the horse broke. He has fallen back into Alesia of the Mandubii, on its hill between two rivers, and Caesar has started to dig.
